short: New CNN front end on mouth pixels (0 of 88 prior decoders) but an unrepeated gain (M06 standard); test words sit in the CNN training frames and speakers are seen (M12 behind).
position: The paper [@noda2014lipreading] changes the visual front end (M06): a CNN on mouth images emits 40 phoneme posteriors for a GMM-HMM; no CNN appears among the 88 prior lip-reading decoders (pattern match, Appendix), but a network on lip pixels [@duchnowski1994see], network phoneme posteriors decoded by HMMs [@heckmann2001hybrid] and features learned from mouth regions [@ngiam2011multimodal] all came first. M06 is standard, not ahead: the gain over PCA is one comparison on one test set, without seeds or a named test speaker (Sec. 6.3). Evaluation (M12) is behind: the CNN is trained on shuffled frames of all 300 words (Sec. 5), so the 84 "open-vocabulary" test words are unseen only by the HMM, while read priors hold out whole utterances or speakers [@cox2008challenge]. The strongest confound is supervision: only the CNN features see phoneme labels. "Significantly outperform" (Abstract) has no test statistic.
